To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size of a gradient is determined by a function of the delay between sample and choice and the difference between the sample and choice stimuli; and the shape of a gradient is controlled by the sample and by the choice display.

the difference gradient between the sample and the choice stimulus broadens with increasing delay, and that the gradient can be controlled by the sample, by the choice display, or by some combination of the two.

the gradients of choice stimuli that generalize from the sample are broadened by increasing delays and that the choice stimuli are controlled by the samples in some cases and by features of the displays in other cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the processes of learning and memory, especially as these processes operate in human beings.
the general problem of how the nervous system represents and processes information about the world.
the nature of the information that is used to control behavior in a delayed visual matching-to-sampling task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
delayed matching-to-sample performance in neurological patients is controlled by both the samples and by features of the displays that are available for choice.
the data are consistent with the hypothesis of the existence of a single, general, and flexible memory system, which is used in delayed matching-to-same and delayed matching-to-difference tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurological patients' matching performance was controlled by the samples when the sample and choice stimuli had similar features.
the neurological patients' behavior is stimulus controlled, but that this stimulus control is less specific and less effective than in normal subjects.
neurological patients, like normal subjects, can use a variety of stimulus dimensions to solve delayed matching-to-sample problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gradients of differences between the sample and the choice stimulus are a sensitive index of the degree of stimulus control.
, when a subject's choice behavior is controlled by the sample, the subject's choice is determined by the sample.
the gradients are not simply a measure of memory.
